title.rendered: Edexcel A Level Physics: Syllabus & Key Resources

content.rendered:
Key Summary

  • Offered By Pearson Edexcel: Edexcel A Level Physics builds the mathematical problem-solving and practical analysis skills that Engineering, Physics, Medicine, and Computer Science degrees demand.
  • UAE Students Take The IAL (YPH11): Almost every British curriculum school in Dubai delivers the International A Level: modular, six units, assessed across January, June, and October sittings.
  • Six Units Across Two Years: Four content units (WPH11, WPH12, WPH14, WPH15) plus two written practical-skills units (WPH13, WPH16), with 16 core practicals examined on paper.
  • Grades Use UMS: Unit raw marks convert to UMS out of 600 total. A* requires grade A overall plus 270 of 300 UMS across the three A2 units.
  • Past Papers Are The Highest-Value Resource: Pearson archives, Save My Exams, and Physics And Maths Tutor provide papers, mark schemes, and examiner reports across both specifications.

Most students searching for Edexcel A Level Physics hit the same wall: the official specification is a dense PDF, the revision sites assume you already know which version you sit, and almost nobody explains that two different Edexcel physics qualifications exist. Pick the wrong one, and you revise the wrong papers for months.

This guide fixes that. It covers the International A Level (YPH11) that Dubai schools actually teach, the UK spec (9PH0) for comparison, every unit, the grading system, and where the verified resources live.

Ignite Training Institute tutors A Level Physics students across Dubai through the best A Level Tutors in Dubai and Physics Tutors in Dubai, and this structure comes from that work.

Edexcel A Level Physics At A Glance

Edexcel A Level Physics is offered by Pearson Edexcel, one of the UK’s largest exam awarding bodies. For Dubai and international students, the version delivered in school is almost always the International A Level (IAL) Physics, specification YPH11, first taught from September 2018. It is a modular qualification with 6 units, assessed across three exam sittings each year.

The qualification trains the problem-solving, mathematical reasoning, and practical analysis skills that Engineering, Physics, Medicine, and Computer Science degrees are built on. It leads to A* to E grades and is accepted equivalently with the UK A Level by universities in the UK, US, Canada, Australia, and the UAE.

The UK-based linear version, specification 9PH0, is a separate qualification covered later in this guide. At Ignite Training Institute, most of the A Level Physics students we tutor in Dubai sit the IAL, so this guide leads with it.

Know More About: A-Level Grading System Explained: From A* To E & Beyond

Pearson Edexcel International A Level Physics Syllabus (Topics & Coverage)

The IAL Physics syllabus is organised into six units. Units 1, 2, and 3 make up the International AS year; Units 4, 5, and 6 make up the IA2 year. Two of the six are dedicated practical-skills papers, which is a structural feature the UK spec does not share.

The full statement-by-statement breakdown is published in The Official Pearson Edexcel IAL Physics Specification. The specification includes 16 core practical activities spread across the course, and exam questions can draw on any of them.

Unit 1: Mechanics And Materials (WPH11)

Unit 1 covers motion, forces, Newton’s laws, momentum, moments, work, energy, power, fluids, viscosity, and the mechanical properties of materials including the Young modulus. Three core practicals sit in this unit: determining the acceleration of free fall, the falling-ball viscosity method, and measuring the Young modulus of a material.

This is the foundation unit. Students who leave gaps in resolving forces or in vector reasoning here feel it again in Unit 4, because circular motion and fields build directly on this content.

Unit 2: Waves And Electricity (WPH12)

Unit 2 covers wave properties, refraction, interference, the wave nature of light, and then electric circuits: current, potential difference, resistance, resistivity, internal resistance, and potential dividers. It closes the AS content year alongside Unit 1.

Examiner reports for this content area repeatedly flag the resistivity equation as a mark-loser, with students misreading diameter for cross-sectional area or dropping the unit in the final answer. That level of detail is exactly what unit-focused revision should target.

Unit 3: Practical Skills In Physics I (WPH13)

Unit 3 is a written paper that assesses the practical techniques, data handling, uncertainties, and experimental design linked to the Unit 1 and Unit 2 core practicals. There is no coursework; practical competence is examined entirely on paper.

Students often under-prepare for this unit because it looks smaller. It is shorter and carries fewer marks, but the questions demand precise experimental vocabulary, and vague answers score poorly.

Unit 4: Further Mechanics, Fields And Particles (WPH14)

Unit 4 covers circular motion, momentum in two dimensions, electric and magnetic fields, capacitance, and an introduction to particle physics. It is widely considered the hardest content unit in the qualification because it stacks abstract field concepts on top of demanding mathematics.

A minimum of 36 of the 90 marks in this paper target mathematics at Level 2 or above, so algebraic fluency directly limits the achievable grade.

Unit 5: Thermodynamics, Radiation, Oscillations And Cosmology (WPH15)

Unit 5 covers thermal energy, ideal gases, nuclear decay and radiation, gravitational fields, simple harmonic motion, and cosmology including the life cycle of stars and evidence for the expanding universe. It is the widest-ranging unit by topic count.

The spread is the challenge here. Students comfortable with mechanics often lose marks on the descriptive astrophysics content, and the reverse is just as common.

Unit 6: Practical Skills In Physics II (WPH16)

Unit 6 mirrors Unit 3 at A2 standard, assessing planning, implementation, analysis, and evaluation of experiments linked to the Unit 4 and Unit 5 practicals. Questions frequently ask students to identify realistic sources of error and suggest genuine improvements, which rewards students who actually engaged with the practicals rather than memorising write-ups.

Know More About: A Level Subjects: Full List, Combinations & How To Pick?

Edexcel A Level Physics Paper Structure

The IAL is built from six unit papers, each externally examined, with no coursework. The modular structure lets students sit units across January, June, and October series, bank results, and re-sit individual units with the best result counting toward certification.

International A Level Physics (YPH11): 6 Units

The full International A Level requires all six units. The table below shows the verified format of each paper, taken from Pearson’s official IAL science guide.

Each content paper (Units 1, 2, 4, and 5) mixes multiple-choice, short-open, calculation, and extended-writing questions, including a starred six-mark question marked for linkage of ideas. Cash-in code YPH11 is entered when a student wants the full A Level awarded.

International AS Level Physics (XPH11): 3 Units

The International AS is a standalone qualification built from Units 1, 2, and 3. It can be certificated on its own with cash-in code XPH11, or banked as the first half of the full A Level, contributing 50 percent of the total.

Many Dubai schools enter students for the IAS at the end of Year 12, which locks in banked unit results before the IA2 year begins. Understanding Why Choose A Levels? Advantages & Disadvantages Explained helps families see where this AS stage fits in the wider pathway.

A Note On The UK A Level Physics (9PH0)

The UK A Level Physics, specification 9PH0, first taught September 2015, is a separate linear qualification used in UK domestic schools. All assessment lands at the end of Year 13 in the May/June series.

Paper 1 and Paper 2 are each 1 hour 45 minutes and 90 marks, worth 30 percent each. Paper 3 is 2 hours 30 minutes and 120 marks, worth 40 percent, and it is synoptic with a heavy practical focus.

The 9PH0 course is built around 13 topics and carries a separately reported Science Practical Endorsement graded Pass or Not Classified. A minimum of 40 percent of marks across the three papers goes to Level 2 mathematics.

There are no unit re-sits on this route; a retake means re-sitting the full qualification. Full details sit on The Official Pearson Edexcel UK A Level Physics Page.

The infographic below puts these differences side by side in one view. Save it or share it with your school WhatsApp group before anyone buys the wrong revision guide.

For UAE students, the practical takeaway is simple: confirm with your school’s exam officer which specification you are entered for before you download a single past paper. Revising 9PH0 papers for a YPH11 exam wastes weeks.

Know More About: Edexcel Vs Cambridge: Key Differences You Should Know

Edexcel A Level Physics Grade Boundaries

Grade boundaries are the minimum raw marks needed for each grade in a given exam session. Raw boundaries move every session based on paper difficulty, which is why Pearson publishes Official Pearson Grade Boundary Documents after every series. The IAL smooths these shifts through the Uniform Mark Scale (UMS).

How Does The IAL Grading System Work?

Each unit’s raw mark converts to a UMS mark, and the six unit UMS scores combine into a total out of 600 for the full A Level. The content units (1, 2, 4, 5) carry double the weight of the practical units (3 and 6), matching their 20 percent versus 10 percent share of the qualification.

Certification grades follow the standard IAL UMS scale: A at 480 of 600, B at 420, C at 360, D at 300, and E at 240.

The A* is awarded at full cash-in to students who reach grade A overall and score at least 270 of the 300 UMS available across Units 4, 5, and 6 combined. A strong AS year alone cannot earn the A*.

UK A Level Physics Grade Boundaries: June 2026

Pearson has published the June 2026 boundaries for the UK linear spec, and they are worth pinning down. For 9PH0, the A* sat at 239 of 300 raw marks, just under 80 percent, with a pass (E) at 85.

These raw boundaries apply to the June 2026 series only and will move again next session. AS grades run A to E; the A* exists only at full A Level. Source: the official Pearson GCE boundaries document for June 2026.

IAL Physics Unit Grade Boundaries: June 2026

Pearson has also released the June 2026 raw boundaries for the IAL units, in the separate International A Level document. These are the main unit papers; AS units carry no a* (a theoretical a* is published for A2 units only).

Read the Unit 4 row carefully: an a needed 76 of 90 raw marks in June 2026. High boundaries mean the paper was accessible, not that marking was lenient, so accuracy mattered more than difficulty on that sitting.

Two cautions. Modified variants of each unit (1A, 2A and so on) carry slightly different raw boundaries in the same document, so match your exact entry code. And these raw figures apply to June 2026 only; UMS conversions stay fixed, which is why targets are best set in UMS.

Where Do You Find Verified Session Boundaries?

Raw unit boundaries for each January, June, and October series are published only in Pearson’s official boundary documents, and they genuinely change between sessions. We deliberately do not reprint session-specific raw numbers here, because a student revising against last October’s boundary can mis-set their target by several marks.

Before setting target marks, download the latest boundaries release for your exact session and unit codes. Our companion guide on A Level Maths Grade Boundaries Explained: A Number’s Guide walks through reading these documents line by line, and the method transfers directly to Physics.

Know More About: A-Level Grading System Explained: From A* To E & Beyond

How Should You Use Edexcel A Level Physics Past Papers?

Past papers are the highest-value resource in this subject, but most students use them wrongly: too early, untimed, and without the mark scheme. The students who convert practice into grades treat the mark scheme and the examiner report as half the resource, not an afterthought.

Pearson’s published examiner reports for Physics reveal the same patterns year after year. Calculation questions score significantly better than explanation questions. On three-mark “explain” questions, most students make one valid point and stop, leaving two marks unclaimed. And under time pressure, students lose marks not by forgetting equations but by selecting the wrong one for the situation.

That pattern dictates the method. Master a topic first, then attempt its past questions closed-book, then mark ruthlessly against the official scheme, noting whether each lost mark was conceptual, mathematical, or a phrasing gap. Mark schemes teach the exact wording examiners reward, and physics mark schemes are unusually specific about it.

On timing, our position from tutoring IAL students in Dubai is clear: start full past papers in the second term of each year, not the third. Second-term starts leave enough sessions to fix the error patterns the papers expose. Third-term starts only document them. The full weekly method sits in our physics study guide linked below.

Know More About: How To Study Physics Effectively: A Smart Study Plan

Resources For Edexcel A Level Physics

The resources below are the ones we point A Level Physics students to at Ignite Training Institute. Official Pearson links are the source of truth; the third-party archives are practice support.

1. Official Edexcel Resources

These are the primary sources for the specification, sample assessments, and boundaries. Verify anything important here first.

  • The Official Pearson Edexcel IAL Physics Specification covers YPH11 and XPH11 in full, including all 16 core practicals.
  • The Official Pearson Edexcel UK A Level Physics Page holds the 9PH0 specification and its sample assessment materials.
  • Official Pearson Grade Boundary Documents publish raw and UMS boundaries after every series.

2. Past Papers And Mark Schemes

Official papers come from Pearson directly; recent series are restricted to exam centres, while older series are open.

  • Pearson’s Official Past Papers Search is the authoritative archive for both specifications.
  • Save My Exams IAL Physics Past Papers organises IAL papers and mark schemes by year and session.
  • Physics And Maths Tutor Edexcel A Level Physics Revision focuses primarily on the UK 9PH0 spec, with papers sorted by paper number.

3. Topic-Wise Practice Questions

Topic-tagged questions are the most efficient format for attacking a specific weak area such as capacitance or uncertainties.

  • Revisely Edexcel A Level Physics Questions sorts past questions by topic for the UK spec.
  • Physics And Maths Tutor IAL Unit Revision Pages collect notes and unit-level questions for the IAL route.

4. Examiner Reports

The most underused resource in the subject. Each report lists the exact mistakes that cost marks in that session, written by the people who set the papers. They sit alongside the mark schemes in Pearson’s Official Past Papers Search, filed per unit and series.

Know More About: Edexcel IGCSE Physics 4PH1 Specification & Syllabus

Exam Preparation Tips For Edexcel A Level Physics

The students who reach A and A* on this qualification follow a recognisable pattern. The eight tactics below are the ones that consistently move grades across the IAL cohort we tutor at Ignite each year.

1. Plan your unit sittings early. The modular structure is an advantage only if you use it. Sitting Units 1 and 2 in January or June of Year 12 banks results and frees the A2 year for the harder Units 4 and 5.

2. Treat the practical units as real papers. Units 3 and 6 carry 30 percent of the qualification between them. Learn the precise experimental vocabulary: precision, accuracy, uncertainty, and error mean different things, and mixing them costs marks.

3. Drill equation selection, not equation recall. The exam supplies a formulae list. Marks come from choosing the right relationship for an unfamiliar context, so practise deciding which principle applies before touching numbers.

4. Develop every “explain” answer fully. Examiner reports show most students make one valid point on three-mark explanation questions. Train yourself to write cause, mechanism, and consequence as separate marked points.

5. Carry units and signs through every line. Misread diameters, dropped units, and sign errors are the recurring calculation losses in published reports. A one-line symbol list at the start of each question prevents most of them.

6. Keep a mistake log by error type. Conceptual, mathematical, misread, or phrasing. After three weeks the pattern is obvious, and fixing two error types is faster than revising everything twice.

7. Time Unit 4 and Unit 5 strictly. At 90 marks in 105 minutes, the pace is just over a minute per mark. Practise full papers to time in the final six weeks, with only the formulae list and your calculator.

8. Pair Physics with Maths where possible. With a minimum of 36 mathematics marks in each of Units 4 and 5, students also taking Edexcel A Level Maths: Syllabus, Past Papers & Grades carry a measurable speed advantage into the exam.

Know More About: How To Get A* In A-Level With These Proven Tips

Ignite Training Institute: Edexcel A Level Physics Tutors In Dubai

A Level Physics is where capable students most often stall quietly. The step up from IGCSE is real, the field concepts in Unit 4 arrive fast, and one shaky foundation topic can cap every unit built on it. Structured, specification-aligned support closes that gap earlier and more cheaply than a Year 13 rescue.

One student who worked with our tutors across Maths, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology went on to secure A* grades in all four subjects, at both IGCSE and A Level. Families often start with our IGCSE Tutors In Dubai for the 4PH1-to-A-Level bridge, which is where the strongest Year 12 starts are built.

FAQs

1. How Many Papers Are There In Edexcel A Level Physics?

The International A Level (YPH11) has six unit papers: WPH11 to WPH16, sat across January, June, and October series. The UK A Level (9PH0) has three papers, all sat together in May/June at the end of Year 13, plus a separately reported practical endorsement.

2. Is Edexcel IAL Physics The Same As UK A Level Physics?

No, they are different specifications. The IAL (YPH11) is modular with six units, three exam sittings a year, and unit-level re-sits. The UK spec (9PH0) is linear with three terminal papers and a practical endorsement. Universities accept both equivalently, but the papers are not interchangeable for revision.

3. Is Edexcel A Level Physics Hard?

It is one of the most demanding A Level subjects, mainly because it combines abstract concepts with heavy mathematics: Units 4 and 5 each award at least 36 of 90 marks for Level 2 maths. The modular IAL structure softens the load by spreading exams across sittings, and structured past paper work makes the grade manageable.

4. What Is The Pass Mark For Edexcel A Level Physics?

Grade E is the minimum pass, set at 240 of 600 UMS at full IAL cash-in. Raw marks needed per unit change every session, so always check the official Pearson boundary document for your exact series rather than relying on a previous session’s numbers.

5. Can I Resit Edexcel A Level Physics Units?

Yes, on the IAL. Individual units can be re-sat in any later January, June, or October series, and the best result counts toward certification. On the UK 9PH0 spec there are no unit re-sits; retaking means sitting all three papers again in a later June series.

6. Do You Need A Level Maths For Edexcel Physics?

It is not formally required, but it helps significantly. Each IAL content unit awards a minimum share of marks to Level 2 mathematics, and the UK spec awards at least 40 percent across its three papers. Most students who reach A* in Physics also take A Level Maths.

7. How Many Core Practicals Are In Edexcel A Level Physics?

The IAL specification includes 16 core practical activities across the course, examined through the written papers, especially Units 3 and 6. The UK 9PH0 spec also carries 16 core practicals, assessed through written questions and the separately reported Science Practical Endorsement.

8. Where Can I Find Edexcel A Level Physics Past Papers?

Pearson’s official past papers archive is the authoritative source for both specifications, with recent series restricted to exam centres. Save My Exams organises IAL papers well, and Physics And Maths Tutor covers the UK spec thoroughly. Always match the paper’s specification code to your own before practising.

Conclusion

Edexcel A Level Physics comes down to a few clear facts. Dubai students almost always sit the modular IAL (YPH11) with six units across three sittings a year, while the UK 9PH0 is a separate linear qualification.

Grades run A* to E through the UMS system, the 16 core practicals are examined on paper, and the mark schemes and examiner reports are where the real grade gains hide.

If your child is starting Year 12 Physics or needs to recover a weak unit before the next sitting, Book A Free Demo Class or Speak With An Academic Advisor at Ignite, and we will map the unit-sitting plan around your school’s timetable.
